intro: Here the angle is measured from north.

widget.instructions: East is +x and north is +y. Tick Components to split the force along the axes.

stem: A {{F}} N force acts at {{alpha}}° west of north. Take east as +x and north as +y.
What is its x-component? Include the sign.

hints.text: Sketch it: the force leans left of the north axis. Which way does its x-component point?
The given angle is measured from the y-axis, so the x-component is the side opposite that angle.
F_x = −F sin α (negative, because it points west).

component-sign-dropped.text: The size is right, but the force leans west, so its x-component is negative.

sin-cos-swap.text: The angle is measured from north, not from the x-axis. The x-component is opposite that angle: F sin α, with a minus sign for west.

tan-for-component.text: tan relates the two components to each other. Use sin α for the side opposite the angle.

sign-error.text: Check the direction: west of north means the force has a westward (negative x) part.

dimension-mismatch.text: A component of a force is a force, in newtons.

generic.text: Find which side is opposite the {{alpha}}° angle, then decide its sign.

workedSolution.text: The force is {{alpha}}° from the +y axis, leaning west.
The x-component is opposite the angle: size F sin α = {{F}} × sin {{alpha}}° = {{mag}} N. It points west, so F_x = {{Fx}} N (and F_y = +{{Fy}} N).

component-sign-dropped.front: A force points west of north. Sign of its x-component (east positive)?

sin-cos-swap.front: Force F at θ above the x-axis: x-component?
sin-cos-swap.back: F cos θ (adjacent). The y-component is F sin θ.

tan-for-component.front: Does F tan θ give a component of F?
tan-for-component.back: No. tan θ = F_y ÷ F_x relates the components to each other.

generic.front: Angle measured from the y-axis: which ratio gives F_x?
generic.back: sin (the x-component is opposite that angle).

accessibility.altText: A {{F}} N force on a grid, {{alpha}}° to the west of the north axis.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Tick Components and read the description; type your answer in the box.
